messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: row.names in a_ply vs. d_ply
parts:
a_ply preserves original row names, while d_ply starts each group from 1.

I'd think that either both should preserve them, or neither should. Am I missing something?

          -s

> df <- data.frame(a=c(1,2,1),b=c(2,2,2))
> df
  a b
1 1 2
2 2 2
3 1 2

> a_ply(df,1,dput)
structure(list(a = 1, b = 2), .Names = c("a", "b"), row.names = 1L, class = "data.frame")
structure(list(a = 2, b = 2), .Names = c("a", "b"), row.names = 2L, class = "data.frame")
structure(list(a = 1, b = 2), .Names = c("a", "b"), row.names = 3L, class = "data.frame")
> dput(llply(alply(t2,1),row.names),,NULL)
list(`1` = "1", `2` = "2", `3` = "3")

> d_ply(df,.(a),dput)
structure(list(a = c(1, 1), b = c(2, 2)), .Names = c("a", "b"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -2L), vars = "a")
structure(list(a = 2, b = 2), .Names = c("a", "b"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -1L), vars = "a")
> dput(llply(dlply(t2,.(a)),row.names),,NULL)
list(`1` = c("1", "2"), `2` = "1")

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: row.names in a_ply vs. d_ply
parts:
Generally, plyr drops row names from data frames (because I don't
think they're a good idea), but keeps them for arrays (because they
have subtly different semantics which somehow do seem ok to me)

Hadley

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Re: row.names in a_ply vs. d_ply
parts:
I think that over-writing row names is a bad thing to do. I always encourage people to create an ID number and enter it themselves, but occasionally I'll get a data set whose order alone is used to tie back to field or lab notes that contain the original data. Such data is one sort away from losing that critical link. It's easy to just do ID <- 1:n but if you have to notice that it's missing, which is admittedly rare.

Bob
